subject: Human Evolution
title: Gut Microbiome
description: A short lesson to help you apply Gut Microbiome.

hook.text: Your gut holds trillions of bacteria—more microbial cells than human cells. They're not passengers; they're crew.

buildup.text: Gut microbes digest fiber, produce vitamins, and train the immune system from infancy.

discovery.text: Hunter-gatherer microbiomes are far more diverse than Western ones. Modern diets shrank the ecosystem.

twist.text: Lost microbial diversity correlates with rising obesity, allergies, and autoimmune diseases.

climax.text: We co-evolved with our gut bacteria. Disrupting that partnership has consequences we're just now seeing.

punchline.text: Your oldest allies live in your intestines.

quiz.question: Why is gut microbiome diversity important?
options: Diverse microbes aid digestion, immunity, and overall health
